title: moved mkdocs bibliography hook from top-level hooks/ into docs/hooks/
body:
Keeps the repository root clean by grouping the hook with the rest of the documentation. Since mkdocs copies every non-Markdown file in docs_dir into the generated site, docs/hooks/ is excluded via exclude_docs so that neither bibliography.py nor its __pycache__ get published.

The hook resolves papers.bib through config["docs_dir"], so relocating the file does not affect its behaviour. It is now also covered by the docs/** glob in REUSE.toml.

title: Inconsistent current-operator norms between tJ and tJDistributed
body:
Hi,

When computing the ground-state properties of a t-J model using the xdiag_distributed library, I encountered a critical inconsistency.

For exactly the same physical setup — a 16-site square lattice with one hole, i.e. N_\uparrow = 8 and N_\downarrow = 7 — the serial tJ block and the MPI-parallel tJDistributed block produce identical ground-state energies E0. However, when I apply the same current operator to the corresponding ground-state vectors, the resulting norms (or expectation values) differ drastically.

This leads to completely different physical results, even though the only difference between the two versions of the code is the block definition:
auto block = tJ(N, nup, ndn); versus auto block = tJDistributed(N, nup, ndn);

I am not yet sure where the bug is, but based on the identical energies and the strongly different operator results, it seems that either the wavefunction or the operator application may be handled inconsistently between tJ and tJDistributed.

I have attached a minimal reproducible example in the appendix.

[main.cpp](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/26322994/main.cpp)

I've been trying out the new sparse matrix capabilities in the new release. In some cases, when the sparse matrix construction fails, the error messages seem a bit unclear. In particular, I get the following error:

>nnz: -1643425960

title: Problem to obtain symmetry groups when there are sublattice sites
body:
### Discussed in https://github.com/awietek/xdiag/discussions/63
Originally posted by **angkunwu** June 11, 2025 I was trying to solve an interacting problem in a honeycomb lattice with A, B sublattice sites. Namely, the number of sites Nsite=2*Nx*Ny. When trying to form permutation groups by translations, there are only N=Nx*Ny translations/permutations. The function PermutationGroup() was trying to assign an Nsite-element array to 1*N destination. I wonder if there are ways to form permutation groups with elements less than the number of sites. For instance, a simple case " p1 = Permutation([1, 2, 3, 4]) p2 = Permutation([3, 4, 1, 2]) C = PermutationGroup([p1, p2]) " Right now it gives a dimension mismatch error. If we define extra permutations " N = 10 T = Permutation(circshift(1:N, -2)) # define cyclic group C_N = PermutationGroup([T^k for k in 0:(N-1)]) " The system will abort. Is there a construction to create a proper group? Or is it a missing functionality in the current version? Thank you very much!

title: apparently unexpected behaivour of operator logic
body:
Hello

I am computing some expectation values like so:

```
auto S_zz = OpSum(...)
auto S_zz_c = hc(S_zz);

auto stateT = apply(S_zz, gs);
XDIAG_SHOW(stateT.block());
auto stateA = apply(S_zz_c, stateT);
XDIAG_SHOW(stateA.block());
XDIAG_SHOW(gs.block());
XDIAG_SHOW(stateA.block()==gs.block());

auto a0 = dotC(stateA, gs);
```

The program fails because XDiag throws **Cannot form dot product for states on different blocks**

The output, however, is 

> stateA.block():
> Spinhalf:
>   nsites   : 18
>   nup      : 9
>   irrep    : defined with ID f2888187778d3443
>   dimension: 2,700
>   ID       : 1bf499b5b95b3ded
> 
> gs.block():
> Spinhalf:
>   nsites   : 18
>   nup      : 9
>   irrep    : defined with ID f2888187778d3443
>   dimension: 2,700
>   ID       : 1bf499b5b95b3ded
> 
> stateA.block()==gs.block():
> 0


So the blocks, irreps, etc. are the same, but somehow the basis is not? Seeing as the `==` operator is defined as

```
bool Spinhalf::operator==(Spinhalf const &rhs) const {
  return (nsites_ == rhs.nsites_) && (nup_ == rhs.nup_) &&
         (irrep_ == rhs.irrep_) && (*basis_ == *rhs.basis_);
}
```

Circumventing the apply logic yields reasonable results.
